# TableIQ

> TableIQ is a free, open-source (AGPL-3.0-only) database client for macOS, built in Rust on Tauri. It browses, queries and edits PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite and DuckDB, has dedicated browsers for MongoDB and Redis, reads ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Turso/libSQL, rqlite, Meilisearch, Qdrant, InfluxDB 3, Chroma and Weaviate over HTTP, and connects to Postgres- and MySQL-compatible products such as CockroachDB, TiDB, YugabyteDB, TimescaleDB, Neon and Supabase. A local MCP server lets coding agents such as Cursor, Claude Code and Claude Desktop query only the connections the user shares, read-only by default, and logs every call in MCP Activity. Made by Ideolyst.

Key facts:

- Platform: macOS, one universal app for Apple silicon and Intel. The signed Mac download is not yet available; the planned release supports Apple silicon and Intel.
- Price: free. Every engine, the MCP server and its guard, bring-your-own-key AI, staged edits, SSH tunnels, unlimited connections and every feature in the first public release stay free. No engine or device-count paywall.
- Agents: MCP over HTTP on 127.0.0.1 with a bearer token. Writes are refused unless the user allows them per connection. Read-only access can still expose sensitive data or run expensive queries; use a least-privilege database role.
- Editing: changes stage in the grid, the user reviews the exact SQL, and they commit in one transaction. Production-tagged connections confirm every commit.
- Privacy: no account and no required cloud service. Credentials are stored in the macOS Keychain. Built-in AI sends context only to the provider the user configures, when used.
- Beta: compatible products not yet verified against the live product are labelled Beta (Amazon Redshift, Apache Doris, SelectDB, Manticore Search, PlanetScale, Neon, Supabase, AlloyDB, Amazon RDS/Aurora, Azure Database, Google Cloud SQL).

- [Understand MCP permissions](https://tableiq.ideolyst.com/guides/mcp-permissions.html): connection sharing, tokens, refused writes and engine-specific limits
